questions.subject: STATISTICS
questions.stem: A clinician's note: n=49, SD=7, z*=2. ME? A solution note warns that 2*7 would forget sqrt(n). Diagnose that error and report the correct value.
questions.explanation: ME=2*7/sqrt(49)=2*7/7=2. Using 2*7 would forget sqrt(n). Margin of error equals the critical value multiplied by the standard error, so it scales with both confidence and sampling noise. Confusing the margin with the full interval width is the typical error.

questions.subject: STATISTICS
questions.stem: A clinician's note 95% CI for mean is (5,15). Which is wrong? "We are 95% confident true mean is in (5,15)" is the answer a classmate submitted. Diagnose the mistake in that choice, then select the option that is fully correct.

options.text: We are 95% confident true mean is in (5,15)
options.misconception: Treats we are 95% confident true mean is in (5,15) as the keyed result when a different choice is correct.

options.text: Method captures true mean 95% of the time
options.misconception: Treats method captures true mean 95% of the time as the keyed result when a different choice is correct.
Treats interval estimates the true mean as the keyed result when a different choice is correct.

questions.explanation: The CI is for the true mean, not for sample means. Options A, C and D are correct interpretations; B misinterprets the interval as a statement about the distribution of sample means rather than about the population mean. The correct choice is B because it is the only statement that misreads the interval: a confidence interval describes the population mean and the long-run behaviour of the method, not the distribution of sample means. Options A, C and D are all sound interpretations.
